newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Resolute looks to 400,000 oz production.
newsitem.headline: Resolute looks to 400,000 oz production.

text.p: Resolute Ltd said on Friday it was budgeting attributable gold production of about 400,000 ounces in 1997/98 to June 30, up from its record 292,492 ounces in 1996/97, with half coming from its Chalice and Obotan mines.

In its June quarter report, Resolute said Chalice, 60 km north west of Norsesman in Western Australia, was currently one of Australia's most profitable operations with June quarter cash costs of US$133 per ounce.

The Obotan gold project in Ghana, where the first gold pour took place a month ahead of schedule in May 1997, was similarly forecast to have low cash costs, under US$220 an ounce, it said. "These two low cost mines alone will contribute half of the 400,000 ounce production target in fiscal 1997/98," it said.
Resolute, which achieved average cash costs of A$382 per ounce in 1996/97, said its share of cash costs in 1997/98 was forecast to be around A$350 an ounce.
The company said it proposed combining the operations of Chalice with nearby Higginsville, with Higginsville ore being trucked and treated at the currently underutilised Chalice mill.

"It is presently estimated that operational savings will be significant whilst at the same time materially increasing Chalice mine life," it said, adding that the Higginsville mill could be moved to one of Resolute's new development projects.
Resolute said it achieved record total production of 105,492 ounces in the June quarter, up 28 percent from the previous quarter's total of 82,199 ounces.
Attributable production rose 26 percent to a record 87,213 ounces compared with the previous quarter's 69,170.
Resolute said significant reductions in cash costs were achieved in the quarter, with costs from all mines averaging A$364 an ounce, down 15 percent on the previous quarter's A$426.
Group attributable cash costs were down to A$391 an ounce from A$449 an ounce, while cash costs for the Chalice mine in Western Australia were A$183 per ounce for the quarter.

The company said 1996/97 total production, including all production from part owned operations, was a record 350,646 ounces, a 19 percent rise on the previous year, at an average cash cost of A$382 per ounce.
